title: The Talladega Transaxle: '69 Mid-Engine Concept
subtitle: The Cancelled '69 Supercar Study
summary: A radical, mid-engine concept fusing Ford's low-drag 1969 Torino Talladega aero nose with a mid-mounted 427 'Cammer' SOHC V8 and GT40 Hewland transaxle.
narrative: HISTORICAL DISCLAIMER: This vehicle concept, narrative, and historical background are entirely fictional. 'Project 69-M' is an alternate-history design study exploring a 'what if' crossover between Ford's NASCAR aero program and Le Mans mid-engine architecture.

This single prototype is all that remains of 'Project 69-M,' Ford's radical, black-budget attempt to rewrite the rules of both NASCAR and the street. The concept was a direct fusion: take the low-drag, extended nose and flush grille of the homologation-bound 1969 Torino Talladega[cite: 1] and mount it on a mid-engine chassis.

While the race cars would always be front-engine (NASCAR rules demanded it), Ford planned to sell 500 mid-engine 'T-Transaxles' as a production vehicle, creating an exotic 'aero-king' to beat Ferrari on the street and Dodge on the high banks. The large mid-body intakes, seen on the production C8 Corvette-like profile, were designed to feed a planned massive mid-ship powertrain.

To explain its mid-engine architecture, Ford engineers created the ultimate 'what if' setup: They took a race-ready 7.0-liter (427 cu in) Ford 'Cammer' SOHC V8, but instead of mounting it in the front, they reversed it, mounting it directly behind the driver. The original Ford Toploader transmission was scrapped. Instead, the 'Cammer' was mated to a custom-cast, heavy-duty Hewland LG transaxle—the same reliable box used in Ford's GT40 program[cite: 3].

This '69 prototype, thus, wasn't just a styling exercise; it was an authentic integration of Ford's two greatest performance eras, pairing the high-drag oval-track nose with the mid-ship transaxle of Le Mans[cite: 1]. The modern, 5-spoke alloys and updated side intakes were added decades later during a modern sympathetic restoration, preparing it for a single, high-speed test run on the gravel road of the skunkworks' private facility.
